transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, my work physical is basically what got me here. The doctor doing the exam said my weight is too low. 

I don't really see the issue, honestly. To me, I just feel... I don't know, lighter on my feet when I play basketball. And I'm not as weighed down when I'm working under cars at the garage. But they told me I needed to come see someone about it, so here I am.
Are you afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat?

I mean... yeah, I guess I am. If I see the scale bump up even just a pound, or if my jeans start feeling tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft. I just worry that it means I'll be slower moving around the cars at the shop, or going up and down the court. I really don't want that to happen.
Have you had episodes when you felt unable to control how much you were eating?

No, not really. I mean, I keep a pretty tight grip on what I eat. I don't think I've ever just... lost control and eaten a bunch of food, if that's what you're asking. I stick to my routine pretty strictly, so that hasn't been an issue for me.
Has a doctor told you that your current weight is significantly below what would be expected for someone your height and age?

Yeah, like I mentioned when we first started talking, that's exactly what the doctor at my work physical said. He told me my weight is way too low for a guy my size and age. But honestly, I just don't see it as a problem. To me, I just feel lighter on my feet when I'm playing basketball, and I'm not all weighed down when I'm sliding under cars at the garage. But yeah, a doctor did tell me that, which is basically why I'm sitting here.
